reasoning: Minnesota’s most recent state-specific general-election polling found Democrats ahead in the Senate race by about 7 points, with Mason-Dixon and campaign polling summarized in late July showing Craig or Flanagan leading Tafoya by roughly that amount. A broader polling average compiled through early August also shows Democrats ahead by 3.5 points, but the most directly relevant general-election state polling in the last 45 days clusters closer to a D+7 margin. Minnesota’s statewide Cook Partisan Voting Index is D+7.

sources.name: Minnesota Reformer
sources.details: Mason-Dixon polling summarized that a generic Democrat led a generic Republican by 8 points, 49% to 41%, and that both Angie Craig and Peggy Flanagan led Michele Tafoya by around 7 points when names were assigned.

sources.name: Native News Online / Public Policy Polling
sources.details: Public Policy Polling found Peggy Flanagan leading Angie Craig 46% to 32% in the Democratic Senate primary; this is primary-only and does not measure the general-election margin.

sources.name: KSTP / SurveyUSA
sources.details: SurveyUSA/KSTP reporting showed the Democratic Senate primary tied and Michele Tafoya leading the Republican primary; this is primary-only and not a general-election measurement.

sources.name: PollsMax polling average
sources.details: A polling average of publicly released Minnesota Senate polls showed Democrats at 48.0% and Republicans at 44.5%, for a D+3.5 average margin.
